Responsive Use of AI Tools

Use of AI Tools

You are welcome—and encouraged—to use AI tools in this course. They can assist with brainstorming ideas, debugging code, improving documentation, and exploring alternative approaches.

However, using AI solely to generate answers or code that you do not fully understand is not permitted. If you submit an assignment, project, or report as your own work, you must be able to demonstrate a thorough understanding of all content, including any code or explanations produced with AI assistance.

Failure to demonstrate understanding may be treated as academic dishonesty (cheating).

For example: Acceptable Uses of AI

  • Using AI to brainstorm project ideas and then refining them with your team.

  • Asking AI to help debug code you have already written, while learning why errors occur.

  • Using AI to improve documentation (e.g., making your README clearer and more professional).

  • Exploring alternative approaches suggested by AI and deciding which one fits best.

For Example: Unacceptable Uses of AI

  • Copying and pasting AI-generated code or answers without understanding how they work.

  • Submitting an AI-generated project proposal, report, or presentation without adding your own analysis or input.

  • Using AI to replace teamwork, such as asking it to complete your entire portion of the group project.

  • Claiming AI output as your original work when you cannot explain or defend it.
